descripcion_es: An action that happened before another past action.
resumen: It is formed with had + past participle and makes it clear that something happened before another past moment or action. It is equivalent to the Spanish pluperfect “había hecho”.

filas: The film had started when we arrived.
I hadn't seen her before that day.

explicacion.texto: Compare: When I got to the station, the train left (the train left when I arrived) with When I got to the station, the train had left (the train had already gone). The past perfect shows the order of events.

items: Va a menudo con when, by the time, before, after, already, just, never… before: By the time the police arrived, the thieves had escaped.
With after or before the order is already clear and the past simple is often enough: After she finished/had finished dinner, she went out.
For causes or explanations of a past situation: He was nervous because he had never flown before.
The contraction 'd can be had or would: I'd finished (had) / I'd go (would).

explicacion.texto: Don't overuse it: if you tell the events in the order they happened, use the past simple. The past perfect is only needed when you go back in time.

ejemplos.frase: When I opened the fridge, someone had eaten my cake.
ejemplos.traduccion: Cuando abrí la nevera, alguien se había comido mi tarta.

ejemplos.frase: She had never seen the sea until she was twenty.
ejemplos.traduccion: No había visto nunca el mar hasta que cumplió veinte años.

ejemplos.frase: By the time we got there, the shop had closed.
ejemplos.traduccion: Para cuando llegamos, la tienda ya había cerrado.

ejemplos.frase: I recognised him because I had met him at a conference.
ejemplos.traduccion: Lo reconocí porque lo había conocido en un congreso.

ejemplos.frase: Had you finished the report before the meeting?
ejemplos.traduccion: ¿Habías terminado el informe antes de la reunión?

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: When I arrived, the meeting has already started.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: When I arrived, the meeting had already started.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: An action before another past action goes in the past perfect, not the present perfect.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I had gone to the cinema yesterday.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I went to the cinema yesterday.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: If there is no other past reference point, the past simple is enough.
After had comes the past participle (gone), not the past simple (went).

ejercicios.frase: When we got to the cinema, the film ___ (already / start).
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the central rule of the card: the past perfect shows that something happened before another past moment. The clue is when we got to the cinema, the reference point, and already, which confirms that the film started earlier. Already goes between had and the past participle: had already started. The contraction 'd is also accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The film started before we arrived: had + already + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Cuando llegamos al cine, la película ya había empezado.

errores_previstos.respuesta: has already started
errores_previstos.explicacion: The present perfect cannot refer to a past moment; you need had.

errores_previstos.respuesta: already started
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past simple does not show the earlier time the sentence requires; had is missing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: had already start
errores_previstos.explicacion: After had comes the past participle started, not the infinitive.

ejercicios.frase: He was hungry because he ___ (not eat) all day.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in Rules and key points: the past perfect explains the cause of a past situation. The clue is he was hungry, a past situation, and because, which introduces an earlier cause. The negative is hadn't + past participle, and eat has an irregular past participle: eaten.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A cause earlier than the past situation: hadn't + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tenía hambre porque no había comido en todo el día.

errores_previstos.respuesta: didn't eat
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past simple does not show that not eating came before being hungry; you need hadn't eaten.

errores_previstos.respuesta: hadn't ate
errores_previstos.explicacion: Ate is past simple; after had comes the past participle eaten.

errores_previstos.respuesta: hasn't eaten
errores_previstos.explicacion: The present perfect does not fit in a past narrative (was hungry).

ejercicios.frase: I didn't know the city because I ___ (never / be) there before.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule of never… before with the past perfect: an experience before a past moment. The clue is I didn't know the city, a past situation, and the cause with never… before. Never goes between had and the past participle, and the past participle of be is been: had never been.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: An experience before a past moment: had never been.
ejercicios.traduccion: No conocía la ciudad porque nunca había estado allí antes.

errores_previstos.respuesta: had never gone
errores_previstos.explicacion: For having visited a place, use been; gone implies that someone went and has not come back.

errores_previstos.respuesta: have never been
errores_previstos.explicacion: The reference point is past (didn't know): had, not have.

errores_previstos.respuesta: never was
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past simple does not express the earlier time; also, never would go before: had never been.

ejercicios.frase: By the time the firefighters arrived, the fire ___ (destroy) the house.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule of by the time with the past perfect, as in By the time the police arrived, the thieves had escaped. The clue is by the time, which shows that, when the firefighters arrived, the destruction was already complete. So had + destroyed (regular past participle).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: By the time shows that the action was already finished: had + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Cuando llegaron los bomberos, el fuego ya había destruido la casa.

errores_previstos.respuesta: destroyed
errores_previstos.explicacion: With by the time the past simple does not make it clear that the destruction had already finished; the past perfect is required.

errores_previstos.respuesta: has destroyed
errores_previstos.explicacion: The reference point is past (arrived): had destroyed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: had destroy
errores_previstos.explicacion: After had comes the past participle destroyed.

ejercicios.frase: When I arrived at the party, Anna ___, so I didn't see her.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the comparison rule in the card: when + past simple versus when + past perfect. The clue is so I didn't see her, which reveals that Anna left before I arrived. So had left; with left it would seem that she left just as I arrived.
ejercicios.traduccion: Cuando llegué a la fiesta, Anna se había ido, así que no la vi.

por_opcion.left: Incorrect here: it would mean that she left at the moment I arrived or just after, which does not fit well with not having seen her.
por_opcion.had left: Correct: Anna's leaving happened before my arrival.
por_opcion.has left: Incorrect: the present perfect cannot be tied to a past moment (when I arrived).

ejercicios.frase: She ___ the door, turned off the lights and went to bed.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's advice “Don't overuse it”: if the events are told in the order they happened, the past simple is enough. The clue is the list of successive actions in the past simple (turned off, went). The first one must be in the same tense: locked.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Actions told in order: past simple.
ejercicios.traduccion: Cerró la puerta con llave, apagó las luces y se fue a la cama.

por_opcion.locked: Correct: actions told in chronological order, all in the past simple.
por_opcion.had locked: Incorrect: the past perfect suggests a step back in time that does not exist here; it breaks the sequence.
por_opcion.has locked: Incorrect: the present perfect does not mix with a narrative sequence in the past.

ejercicios.frase: ___ you ever travelled abroad before you moved to Berlin?
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the “Question” row of the table: had + subject + past participle. The clue is before you moved to Berlin, a past reference point: the question is about experiences before it. So Had, with travelled already in the past participle.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: An experience before another past event (before you moved): Had.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿Habías viajado alguna vez al extranjero antes de mudarte a Berlín?

por_opcion.Have: Incorrect: the present perfect asks about experiences up to now, not up to a past moment like the move.
por_opcion.Did: Incorrect: did goes with the infinitive (Did you ever travel…?), and travelled is a past participle.
por_opcion.Had: Correct: a past perfect question about an experience before another past event.

ejercicios.frase: I couldn't pay because I ___ my wallet at home.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule about causes of a past situation: the earlier cause goes in the past perfect. The clue is I couldn't pay, a past situation, and because, which introduces what happened before. Leaving the wallet happened before not being able to pay: had left.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Leaving the wallet happened before not being able to pay.
ejercicios.traduccion: No pude pagar porque me había dejado la cartera en casa.

por_opcion.had left: Correct: a cause earlier than the past situation.
por_opcion.have left: Incorrect: the present perfect does not fit with couldn't, in the past.
por_opcion.was leaving: Incorrect: the past continuous would mean that I was in the process of leaving it, which makes no sense here.

ejercicios.frase: The train has already left when we reached the platform.
respuestas: The train had already left when we reached the platform.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the first typical mistake in the card: an action before another past action goes in the past perfect, not the present perfect. The clue is when we reached the platform, in the past. Has is present perfect and cannot be tied to a past moment; it must be changed to had.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: An action before another past action: had, not has.
ejercicios.traduccion: El tren ya se había ido cuando llegamos al andén.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The train has already left when we reached the platform.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the sentence without correcting it: with a past reference point you need had.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The train already left when we reached the platform.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past simple does not show that the train left earlier; the idea of “before” is lost.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The train had already leave when we reached the platform.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After had comes the past participle left.

ejercicios.frase: They had took the wrong road.
respuestas: They had taken the wrong road.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the third typical mistake in the card: after had comes the past participle, not the past simple. The clue is took, the past simple of take. Take is irregular with three different forms (take, took, taken), so you must write taken.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Had goes with the past participle: taken.

errores_previstos.respuesta: They had took the wrong road.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the sentence without correcting it: after had comes the past participle taken.

errores_previstos.respuesta: They had take the wrong road.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After had you do not use the infinitive, but the past participle taken.

errores_previstos.respuesta: They have taken the wrong road.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It corrects the past participle but changes the tense to the present perfect for no reason.

ejercicios.enunciado: Join the sentences with “when”, using the past perfect for the earlier action. Begin with “When I got home”.
ejercicios.frase: My flatmate cooked dinner. Then I got home.
respuestas: When I got home, my flatmate had cooked dinner.
When I got home my flatmate had cooked dinner.
When I got home, my flatmate had already cooked dinner.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the central rule: the earlier action goes in the past perfect and the later one in the past simple. The clue is then in the original sentences, which shows that cooking came first and arriving afterwards. Begin with When I got home (past simple) and the earlier action becomes had cooked. Adding already is also accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The earlier action (cooking) goes in the past perfect.
ejercicios.traduccion: Cuando llegué a casa, mi compañero de piso había hecho la cena.

errores_previstos.respuesta: When I got home, my flatmate cooked dinner.
errores_previstos.explicacion: With the past simple it would mean that she started cooking when I arrived, reversing the order.

errores_previstos.respuesta: When I had got home, my flatmate cooked dinner.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past perfect goes on the earlier action (cooking), not on the arrival.

errores_previstos.respuesta: When I got home, my flatmate has cooked dinner.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The present perfect does not fit with a past reference point: had cooked.

ejercicios.enunciado: Turn the sentence into a question.
ejercicios.frase: She had seen the film before.
respuestas: Had she seen the film before?
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the “Question” row of the table: had + subject + past participle. The clue is had in the affirmative sentence: just put it before the subject she, without adding did. The past participle seen and the rest of the sentence do not change.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Did she have seen the film before?
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past perfect does not use did; had goes before the subject.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She had seen the film before?
errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish intonation: a written question requires inverting had and the subject.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Had she saw the film before?
errores_previstos.explicacion: Saw is past simple; the past participle is seen.

respuestas: they had already eaten the cake
had they already eaten the cake
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule for the position of already: it goes between had and the past participle. The clue is that the words include had, already and eaten. The order is subject + had + already + past participle + object. The question, with had before the subject, is also correct.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Already goes between had and the past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ya se habían comido la tarta. (También: ¿Ya se habían comido la tarta?)

errores_previstos.respuesta: they had already the cake eaten
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past participle stays next to the auxiliaries and the object comes after: had already eaten the cake. Putting the object in the middle is a calque from other languages, not English.

errores_previstos.respuesta: they had eaten already the cake
errores_previstos.explicacion: Already cannot separate the verb from its direct object.

respuestas: she had never seen snow before
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule of never… before: never goes between had and the past participle, and before at the end. The clue is that the words include had, never, seen and before. The order is subject + had + never + past participle + object + before.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Subject + had + never + past participle + complement.
ejercicios.traduccion: Nunca había visto la nieve antes.

errores_previstos.respuesta: she had seen never snow before
errores_previstos.explicacion: Never goes between had and the past participle: had never seen, like Spanish “nunca había visto”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: she had never seen before snow
errores_previstos.explicacion: Before goes at the end; it cannot separate the verb from its object.

descripcion_larga_es: The past perfect (had + past participle) is equivalent to the Spanish pluperfect “había hecho” and is used to go back in time within a past narrative: it shows that something happened before another past moment or event. It is key for telling stories clearly and explaining causes. Spanish speakers find it hard not to overuse it, not to confuse it with the present perfect and to use the past participle, not the past simple.

contexto.que_es: It is the tense formed with had and the past participle of the verb. It places an action before another action or a past moment that serves as a reference point, just like the Spanish pluperfect.
contexto.por_que_importa: It shows the order of events: When I arrived, the train left (it left when I arrived) does not mean the same as the train had left (it had already gone). Using it wrongly confuses the chronology of a story. In exams it appears in narratives, in reported speech and in third conditionals.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When there is a reference point in the past and you go back from it, with signals such as when, by the time, before, after, already, just or never… before. Also to explain the cause of a past situation (He was nervous because he had never flown). Spanish speakers tend to use the present perfect instead or, on the contrary, to use it without a past reference point.
